properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 9/27/2021 to EQT ARO LLC in McIntyre Twp, Lycoming county. 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: EQT ARO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 9/27/2021
Violation Code: 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
Violation ID: 931293
Permit API: 081-21877
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: McIntyre Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 9/27/2021
Comments: This follow-up inspection was conducted in order to assess conditions on both well pads. I inspected Pad A first. The 6 wells on Pad A are still in flowback. Multiple batteries of frac tanks are present within secondary containment. The pad was dry and no issues were noted. On Pad B, drilling is on-going. I met with EQT company man RD Mann uppn arriving on location. Five of the nine wells have already been drilled. In the sump on the pad which had been installed after fluid with elevated electrical conductivity (EC), strontium, and aluminum was discovered, the EC was approximately 800 uS/cm. Two areas of staining were found on the pad and the fluid present here had an EC of approximately 800 uS/cm in both areas. Other puddles on the pad had an EC of approximately 500 uS/cm. The Department recommends scraping these stains from the pad surface and disposing of the material appropriately. I showed Mr. Mann the location of these stains during this inspection and he said that he would have both stains scraped immediately. Violations remain outstanding for the diesel mud release on Pad B described in the 8/9/21 inspection number 3231577 by DEP WQS Brad Kline.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 4/06/2022 to REPSOL OIL & GAS USA LLC in Ward Twp, Tioga county. 102.4(b)1 - EROSION AND SEDIMENT CONTROL REQUIREMENTS - Person conducting earth disturbance activity failed to implement and maintain E & S BMPs to minimize the potential for accelerated erosion and sedimentation.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: REPSOL OIL & GAS USA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 4/05/2022
Violation Code: 102.4(b)1 - EROSION AND SEDIMENT CONTROL REQUIREMENTS - Person conducting earth disturbance activity failed to implement and maintain E & S BMPs to minimize the potential for accelerated erosion and sedimentation.
Violation ID: 950794
Permit API: 117-22103
Unconventional: Yes
County: Tioga
Municipality: Ward Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 4/06/2022
Comments: The DEP conducted a routine inspection of Repsol's DCNR 587 02-003 well site located in Ward Township, Tioga County on 4/6/2022 at 1030 hours. The weather was 49 degrees with an overcast and very light rain. Rain fell onsite overnight and is forecasted to rain more later in the day. DEP Environemntal Trainee, Brooke Millisock, assisted me during the inspection. We met with Billy Watts (Repsol) to discuss work that Repsol plans to have done on the access road. During the inspection, a large amount of mud was observed on the access road due to recent rainfall mixing with sediment present on the road. Repsol recently installed 18-inch silt sock along the roadside to prevent further sedimentation off the side of the access road. Today, sediment-laden water was observed discharging into Fellows Creek along the northern shore, below the access road bridge (photos #1, 11 & 12). Sediment-laden water was also observed to be dripping from the bridge into Fellows Creek as truck traffic crossed the bridge. The bridge top is constructed with metal plating and sediment-laden water is seeping through the cracks. Rocks utilized in the construction and stabilization of the bridge (photo #6) were also observed to be covered in a layer of the sediment. Samples 0983-276 & 0983-277 were collected for Standard Analysis Code (SAC) 046 from Fellows Creek both upstream and downstream of the bridge crossing. Repsol had a crew in route to begin cleaning/sweeping the access road and adding a fresh stone layer for truck traffic to drive on. The DEP recommends to continue evaluating the area and maintaining BMPs to contain all possible sediment to the site. Any additional discharges of sediment-laden water into Fellows Creek or outside of the limit-of-disturbance are recommended to be reported to the DEP as/if they occur. Numerous puddles on the pad surface were field measured for electrical conductivity utilizing an Oakton PCSTestr 35. The majority of the puddles field measured today ranged from 1.8mS/cm to 5.3mS/cm. Sample 0983-278 was collected for SAC 942 from a puddle field measured at 5.34mS/cm found near the center of the pad (see photos #8, 9 & 10). The sample results will be analyzed for pollution once reported by the DEP laboratory. The findings of this inspection report were communicated with Meagan DePue (Repsol Environmental) over the phone. Recent E&S inspections conducted by the operator were also requested. Based on the findings of this inspection and the observation of sediment-laden water discharging into Fellows Creek, violations of the following are cited against API #117-22103 at this time: 25 Pa. Code 102.4(b)1 35 P.S. 691.401 We departed the site at 1200 hours.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 3/31/2021 to BKV OPR LLC in Rush Twp, Centre county. 78a91(a) - PLUGGING - GENERAL PROVISIONS - Upon abandoning a well, the owner or operator failed to plug the well to stop the vertical flow of fluids or gas within the well bore under   3221 of the 2012 Oil & Gas Act, 25 Pa. Code    78a.92-78a.98 or an approved alternate method.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: BKV OPR LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 3/31/2021
Violation Code: 78a91(a) - PLUGGING - GENERAL PROVISIONS - Upon abandoning a well, the owner or operator failed to plug the well to stop the vertical flow of fluids or gas within the well bore under § 3221 of the 2012 Oil & Gas Act, 25 Pa. Code §§ 78a.92—78a.98 or an approved alternate method.
Violation ID: 912721
Permit API: 027-21501
Unconventional: Yes
County: Centre
Municipality: Rush Twp
Inspection Type: Plugging(Includes Plugged/Mined Through)
Inspection Date: 3/31/2021
Comments: A follow-up inspection of the Cowfer 1 well was conducted March 31, 2021. At the time of inspection, the operator has removed gravel from the cellar for further evaluation following the detection of gas at surface following plugging operations. The wellhead was removed after plugging ops, and a plate with a 2" vent has been attached to the 9 5/8" casing to evaluate the well after the well was dug up. I met with the operator to evaluate the well at this time. The well was actively venting and foam surrounded the well, thought to be from surfactant used in the borehole conditioning process to remove OBM from the well prior to pumping cement plugs during plugging ops and foaming up from the venting of gas. 100% methane was detected at the well with an Altair 5x gas meter at this time. The well is in violation of 78.91(a) for failure to stop vertical flow of gas within the wellbore upon plugging. Please see violation description and requested response below.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: SWN PROD CO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 08/26/2020
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 892779
Permit API: 081-21794
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: Jackson Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 08/26/2020
Comments: This inspection was conducted in response to a report of a release discovered by the operator on August 22, 2020. DEP EP specialist Justin Abbott accompanied me on this inspection and we were met by Mike Deming of SWN on site. According to Mr. Deming, fluid was found between the layers of the secondary containment near where the blender had been during the recent frac. He said that the containment was removed in this area and puddles of fluid with elevated conductivity (EC) were discovered on the pad surface. He said that a spill of 10 gallons of produced water had been spilled on the secondary containment during the frac in this area and he believed that this release was related. At the time of this inspection, the area impacted by the release had already been excavated. The EC readings in this area on the Hanna soil conductivity meter were all less than 1 mS/cm. Mr. Deming said that approximately 60 tons of material had been excavated in an area approximately 60 ft x 80 ft. He estimated the spill volume at 10 gallons based on this information. Some puddles with EC ranging between 2 to 3 mS/cm were observed on the pad. The puddles were located in travel lanes on the pad. Mr. Deming said that he believed that these were due to the truck traffic bringing magnesium chloride onto the pad because magnesium chloride is used for dust control on the access road. The Department recommends sucking up these puddles as needed.Violations noted and considered immediately corrected.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: STL RESOURCES LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 1/10/2022
Violation Code: 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
Violation ID: 941564
Permit API: 035-21324
Unconventional: Yes
County: Clinton
Municipality: Grugan Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 1/10/2022
Comments: On January 10, 2022, DEP representative Brad Kline conducted a site inspection at STL Resources Sturgis South Pad in response to a spill notification received on January 10, 2022. DEP spoke with Seth Rodriguez with STL Resources. Mr. Rodriguez said that a hose that manifolded multiple frac tanks onsite broke and released approximately 1,600 barrels of production fluid water from frac tanks. There were 17 frac tanks onsite in secondary containment for flow back storage from recent stimulation of the wells on the pad. The secondary containment of the frac tanks was overwhelmed and some of the production fluid water spilled to the pad surface. The amount of production fluid that was spilled to the pad surface is still being calculated. The spill was first noticed on January 8, 2022 but STL Resources failed to notify the DEP emergency spill line. The production fluid ran into a drain on the southwest corner of the well pad which outlets off the pad into a infiltration berm. An area 60 yds. x 40 yds. of the pad surface was impacted by production fluid. Off the pad area of impact was about 20 ft. wide by 120 ft. long. At the time of inspection, STL Resources contractors were vacuuming up the free standing production fluid out of the drainage outlet and the fluid pooled up in front of the infiltration berm. The DEP measured soil conductivity around the area of impact on the well pad and multiple measurements resulted in over range readings of the soil conductivity meter. Soil conductivity off the pad surface where the production fluid water flowed into the infiltration berm also resulted in an over range readings. The maximum conductivity measurement of the soil conductivity meter is 4,000 microsiemens per centimeter. STL Resources have contractors scheduled to arrive today to delineate the area of impact and to remove the impacted soils. Violations of the Clean Streams Law 402(b), Chapter 78a.56(a), Chapter 78a.66(b)2, Solid Waste Management Act Section 301. The DEP recommends STL Resources begin the Act 2 process.

Report Details

Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 964783
Permit API: 117-22124
Unconventional: Yes
County: Tioga
Municipality: Hamilton Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 8/10/2022
Comments: Site inspection conducted to review use of 24,000 barrel Comtech Dynatank Modular Aboveground Storage System (MASS). There are no Repsol personnel on site at time of inspection. Weather conditions are sunny and 68 degrees F. During this inspection, it appears that Repsol is completing flowback operations from stimulation activity during spring of 2022. Nine wells have been drilled in the previous twelve months and there are fifteen wells in production on site at this time. The 24,000 barrel Dynatank on site to facilitate flowback operations remains in place. A loader is working on site to pick up used secondary containment structures for disposal. A water truck is removing fluid from the produced fluid tanks. Well cellars for the 8H and 10H wells are filled to capacity with stormwater and the Department recommends vacuuming out these well cellars. Field conductivity screenings were conducted on the Johnson pad using an Oakton PCTS 50 meter and a Hanna Groline soil conductivity meter. Fluid within secondary containment structures were observed to be less than 1mS/cm. Conductivity readings observed in puddled areas of the pad surface ranged from 3.46-6.26 mS/cm. Field sample 4406-015 was collected from puddled water adjacent to the NW frac tank battery load out area (photos 6 and 7). Conductivity in the area sampled was observed to be 4.22 mS/cm indicating that a potential pollutional event may have occurred. Operator was notified of areas of concern via phone call on 8/10/22. Additional violations may be issued pending results of water sample analysis.

During IR 4139756, Mr. Anderson stated that an updated Emergency Response Plan is expected to be on site within the next 10 days. Violations issued to the 6H gas well for failure to have the ERP on site are being continued at this time.At the time of this inspection, it does not appear that any of the wells at the Cowden well site are in production yet (the 6H, 10H, and 16H). At the time of this inspection, the Department observed a white above ground storage tank on the graveled well pad, the Department did not observe this tank to be connected to gas wells or any other production equipment on the Cowden 16 well pad. At the time of this inspection, the Department also observed additional production equipment that did not appear to be connected to anyother production equipment or any wells on the well pad. At the time of this inspection, a white structure that during IR 4139756 was not observed to be connected to any other production equipment or wells on site was observed to be actively being removed from the gravel well pad. In IR 4139756, the Department requested a written timeline for when all equipment, tanks, and structures not necessary for the production of the well(s) on the Cowden 16 well pad will be removed and when any equipment, tanks and structures necessary for production will be connected. The Department requested this written timeline be provided to the Department by COB 3/13/2026. No response has been received to date.Violations issued to the 6H gas well for failure to remove equipment, tanks, and structures not necessary for the production of the well(s) on the Cowden 16 well pad are being continued at this time as the white structure was the only equipment observed to be removed from the site at this time.At the time of this inspection, the DEP observed a well tag fixed to the 6H gas well with all required information posted on it. No fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near the surface of the 6H gas well at this time.Based on today's inspection, violations issued to the 6H gas well for failure to have ERP on site and for failure to remove production equipment not in use/connected to other equipment or a gas well are being continued at this time.

Comments: This inspection was conducted in response to the notification by Cliff Easton of Consortium Energy of a crude oil release from a buried gathering line located approximately 150 feet to the south of this conventional well.Upon my arrival onsite, Cliff and I evaluated the section of roadside ditch where oil was discovered, which is within approximately ten feet of an unnamed tributary (UNT) of Turnup Run. Comments: This inspection was performed following a report to the NWRO by Diversified Oil and Gas of a 25 gallon brine spill at their #38067 well. It appears as though a small leak formed in a 50 barrel poly tank over the winter, which allowed some production fluid to leach out slowly over time. Once the snow melted, the well tender noticed a small area (~10x10 ft) that had vegetation missing and deer prints. The diking was unlined, so it seems that production water had leached out, and high conductivity levels were noted in this area. All the brine stayed in a small area, and no waters are nearby to be a concern for migration. The operator has shut in this well for the time being, and excavation is scheduled for the week of 4/8. Continued inspection of this site will be performed at that time.

Violation ID: 938553
Permit API: 015-23676
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Springfield Twp
Inspection Type: Administrative/File Review
Inspection Date: 12/07/2021
Comments: The DEP completed an administrative inspection on Blackhill Energy's Kinglsey E 7H well(API 015-23676) located in Springfield Township, Bradford County on 12/7/2021. The inspection was completed in order to summarize sample results from a sample collected during the 11/10/2021 inspection (IR #3282018). On 11/10/2021, I inspected Blackhill Energy's Kingsley E well site and discovered elevated electrical conductivity puddles off of the pad-wide containment. Elevated electrical conductivity puddles were field measured utilizing an Oakton PCSTestr 35 and ranged in field readings from 5.4 to 9.0 mS/cm. A sample for standard analysis code 942 was collected on 11/10/2021 from a puddle field measured at ~7.7mS/cm (0983-254). The sample was later received by the DEP Laboratory in Harrisburg, PA on 11/16/2021 and the final sample results were reported on 12/4/2021. The DEP's analytical sample results are attached as photos and as a file. Additional information regarding the initial inspection can be found in inspection record #3282018. The operator responded immediately after notification of the discovery. The operator believed the containment berms were driven over and crushed, which allowed the elevated electrical conductivity water that was on containment to be spilled off of containment. The operator estimated the back (northeastern) side to be less than 1 gallon while the front (southwestern) side was reported to be less than 4 gallons, but was then mixed with freshwater which was sprayed on the pad for dust control. The operator explained that they planned on remediating the impacted area and placing rig mats in front of the driving areas, so trucks will drive over the rig mats and not over the containment berms. Unconventional: Yes

Municipality: Franklin Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2019-01-22
Comments: On 1/22/2019 at approximately 1100, I conducted an incident response inspection of the Cosgray well site located in Franklin Township, Greene County in response to a reported spill of produced water. On 1/21/2019 at 1400, a valve leak as a mist was noticed by the operator. The operator approximated that less than 40 gallons of produced water released from a GPU as a result. Specialized Professional Services (SPSI) responded to remediate the impacted area. During the 1/22/2019 inspection, the following was observed: * Act 9 sign located at the site entrance was in good condition. * Some secondary containment mechanisms utilized on 4 GPUs but containment appeared unable to hold 110% of the unit storage capacity. * SPSI was on site during the inspection cleaning the GPUs. * Liquid observed in the grated tray between the GPUs. * Well identification tags were not able to be found on any wells. An oil sheen was observed in one well cellar (37-125-27404). * Production fluid tanks were within secondary containment and appeared in good condition. Violations were identified during this inspection and will be assessed to each individual well.
